- Target bonus: 15%
- Equity: 0.35% (targeted, subject to stock plan approval)
- Start date proposed: 2026-03-15 (flexible)

Evan’s question: can we guarantee the grant effective date will be his start date (Mar 15)? I’ve attached the draft offer and the equity grant template we typically use. Any guidance on whether we should:
1) promise a grant date = start date, or
2) say grant will be on the next board-approved grant date and include a short explanation in the offer?

Thoughts? If you want me to hold the DocuSign until legal signs off, I can pause.

Folks —

Quick flag from the recruiter: candidate wants grant dated to start date. We need to align on policy. Key constraints:

- Board grants are typically effective on the date the board signs the grant resolution (we can’t legally backdate to the hire date).
- 409A valuation was performed 2026-02-01; typically FMV is valid for 12 months unless there is a material event (fundraise, major M&A).
- If we can’t grant on Mar 15 (board not meeting), we should offer a clear explanation in the offer: "Option award to be granted subject to Board approval; effective date will be the date of grant as approved by the Board." That avoids implying a guaranteed start-date grant.

Marcus — can you confirm if the 409A valuation covers Mar 15? If yes, strike price will be set at the 02/01 FMV. Markus — legal: are there any additional risks if we explicitly tell the candidate the grant will be for Board approval date rather than start date? Monica — recruiting: do we need to avoid scaring the candidate?

If board meets before Mar 15 we can aim to sign grants then; otherwise I’d prefer to keep the offer simple and truthful and include an expected grant timeline.

Laura
VP, Engineering Hiring
Redwood Inference

Laura / team —

Confirming the 409A dated 2026-02-01 is in place and we currently consider that FMV valid through 2027-01-31 unless a material event occurs. No fundraise on the horizon and no material events booked, so the strike price can be set using the Feb 1 409A for any grant with an effective date prior to the next valuation trigger.

Operationally: our stock admin (Carta) requires board approval to create grants. We have a board meeting provisionally scheduled for 2026-03-18 where we plan to approve the standard quarterly grants. If Evan starts on 2026-03-15 and we don't grant until 2026-03-18, two options:

A) Offer language: "Grant subject to Board approval; expected grant date 03/18/2026." Candidate starts on 03/15; grant’s effective date will be 03/18 and strike price set using 409A 02/01.

B) If we need the grant executed on or before start date, we could run a special written consent for the Board to approve a single grant before the board meeting. That increases coordination and is usually reserved for critical hires. It also incurs an admin/time cost and requires scheduling/external counsel sign-off.

I recommend option A unless hiring leadership (Vivek/Laura) want to make this a special-case priority.

Marcus

Laura / team —

Legal note: Option A (board-approved grant on 03/18) is the cleanest and lowest-risk approach. A few clarifying points to include in the offer template:

- Do not represent grant effective date as the start date. Use: "Any equity awards are subject to approval by the company's Board of Directors and will be effective as of the date of the grant approved by the Board."
- Include a one-line explanation of strike price: "The exercise price will be established in accordance with the company’s 409A valuation in effect as of the grant date."
- If we pursue a written consent for an early grant, counsel will need at least 3 business days to prepare the resolution and get signatures; it is not instantaneous.

Also recommend adding a short FAQ/line to reassure the candidate: "We expect routine quarterly grants; you will receive grant paperwork (Carta + DocuSign) within a few business days of Board approval and prior to finalizing your onboarding in Carta."

If leadership wants us to expedite via written consent, loop in me and JWong and confirm the business rationale for the exception.

-Markus
